# Envarium — Local Development Command Center: complete documentation

# Adapter development guide

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adapter-development/

Add a platform or runtime adapter without crossing Envarium domain boundaries.

Add operating-system or external-tool behavior behind an application-owned
interface. Keep domains platform-neutral and preserve the dependency direction
adapter/transport to application to domain. Do not add OS branches to domain
models, a service locator, or a generic command helper.

An adapter change includes capability detection, typed unavailable/degraded
errors, argument-array execution, cancellation, bounded output, redaction where
data crosses a sink, and tests for success, failure, cancellation, permissions,
and reconciliation. Platform files use explicit Go build tags and must compile
in the Linux and Windows `platform-check` target. Native behavior also runs on
its host in CI.

Process adapters must preserve fingerprint ownership and whole-tree stop.
Port adapters return facts and provenance rather than inferred ownership.
Terminal adapters implement resize, Unicode/ANSI transport, bounded detach,
tree termination, and user-visible output only. Launchers accept only typed
terminal/editor/browser operations; browser targets remain HTTP(S).

Plugin adapters belong out of process and use the public `sdk/plugin` protocol
plus conformance kit. Provider-specific AI code stays under
`internal/agents/providers`; provider output remains untrusted schema input.

Update an ADR before changing an accepted boundary, generate contracts rather
than editing generated files, document the platform matrix, and attach progress
evidence for the phase or vertical slice.

---

# ADR-0001: Modular monolith and domain dependency direction

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0001-modular-monolith/

Keep Envarium cohesive while enforcing bounded-context dependency rules.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Envarium coordinates many local capabilities but ships and evolves as one
coherent product. Premature services would add deployment and consistency costs
without independent scaling or ownership needs.

## Decision

Build one modular Go monolith grouped by bounded context. Dependencies flow
from transports/adapters to application use cases to domain models.
Infrastructure implements ports owned by consuming application packages.
Domains do not read each other's tables and collaborate only through explicit
interfaces or typed events. Composition uses manual constructor injection.

## Consequences

The product remains easy to build and operate while package boundaries stay
enforceable. Cross-domain features require explicit contracts. Architecture
checks will reject forbidden imports and miscellaneous shared packages.

---

# ADR-0002: Go as the local control-plane language

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0002-go-control-plane/

Use one portable systems language for control-plane product behavior.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

The control plane needs portable binaries, concurrency, cancellation, local
systems integration, and predictable idle overhead.

## Decision

Implement domain behavior, application services, lifecycle coordination,
persistence, APIs, CLI, and MCP in current stable Go pinned by the repository.
Use explicit typed code and standard-library capabilities where practical.

## Consequences

One toolchain owns operational behavior and cross-platform adapters can share
contracts. Vue and Tauri remain clients; Rust or TypeScript business logic
cannot become an alternate control plane.

---

# ADR-0003: One Envarium binary with daemon, CLI, and MCP subcommands

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0003-one-binary/

Ship one versioned executable over cohesive internal packages.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Separate executables would complicate versioning, installation, local protocol
compatibility, and desktop sidecar packaging.

## Decision

Ship one primary executable named `envarium`. `cmd/envarium` is a small
composition root; command groups delegate to client or application packages.
The binary exposes daemon, CLI, UI, doctor, and MCP entry points without
centralizing their behavior in one package.

## Consequences

Users install and update one version. Internal packages must remain cohesive so
the deployment unit does not become a god binary. The desktop app bundles or
attaches to a compatible copy of the same executable.

---

# ADR-0004: REST, WebSocket, and OpenAPI transport contracts

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0004-rest-websocket-openapi/

Keep browser and client contracts versioned, generated, and inspectable.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Browser, CLI, desktop, plugin, and agent clients need inspectable contracts,
while logs, events, terminals, and sessions need streaming behavior.

## Decision

Use REST JSON under `/api/v1` for commands and queries and versioned WebSockets
for live streams. OpenAPI is the HTTP source of truth and generates Go transport
types and TypeScript clients. Errors use RFC 9457-style problem details.

## Consequences

Contracts remain browser-friendly and debuggable. Generated code must be
isolated and reproducible. Transport handlers translate requests and responses
only; they cannot own orchestration or infrastructure access.

---

# ADR-0005: SQLite, sqlc, migrations, and file-based log segments

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0005-sqlite-persistence/

Store durable local state transactionally and high-volume logs in bounded files.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Envarium is local-first and needs durable relational state without another
service. High-volume logs should not inflate the transactional database.

## Decision

Use SQLite through a pure-Go driver, typed `sqlc` queries, embedded ordered
migrations, WAL mode, foreign keys, and explicit application transaction
boundaries. Store rotating log bodies as files and their metadata/checksums in
SQLite. Store only keychain references for secrets.

## Consequences

Installation remains self-contained and cross-compilation is practical.
Migrations and generated queries become required quality gates. SQLite is an
internal implementation detail, not a public integration contract.

---

# ADR-0006: Docker SDK observation and Compose CLI lifecycle

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0006-docker-compose-runtime/

Observe Docker through its API and execute lifecycle through the installed Compose CLI.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

The Docker Engine API is strong for inspection, events, logs, and metrics, but
Compose lifecycle semantics also depend on the user's installed plugin,
contexts, credential helpers, and configuration.

## Decision

Use the official Docker Go SDK with API negotiation for observation and live
streams. Use the installed `docker compose` CLI for normalized configuration
and lifecycle execution. Identify projects and services through canonical
Compose labels, never container-name prefixes.

## Consequences

Envarium matches commands users already trust while retaining typed
observation. Command building, execution, config reading, event watching, logs,
metrics, and reconciliation remain focused collaborators. Docker failure cannot
disable non-Docker project behavior.

---

# ADR-0007: Native process ownership and reconciliation

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0007-process-ownership/

Identify and stop managed process trees without trusting stale PIDs.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

PIDs are reused, parent processes can exit before children, and projects may be
started outside Envarium. Treating a stored PID as ownership risks signaling
the wrong process or reporting false state.

## Decision

Start managed commands without a shell by default in an OS process group or Job
Object. Persist run ID, PID, executable, start time, working directory, and
available platform identity evidence. Reconcile using that fingerprint plus
ports and declared service metadata. Gracefully terminate the process tree,
then escalate after a configured timeout. External processes remain observed,
not owned, until adoption is safe and explicit.

## Consequences

Process adapters require platform-specific identity and tree tests. Some live
state remains honestly unknown on constrained platforms. Restart policy is
opt-in and cannot conceal repeated crashes.

---

# ADR-0008: Project manifest precedence and provenance

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0008-manifest-precedence/

Resolve effective project configuration without losing source evidence.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Projects need portable definitions, machine-local values, generated inference,
live discoveries, and one-operation overrides without silently losing the
origin of effective configuration.

## Decision

Resolve each field using, highest first: runtime override,
`.envarium/project.local.yml`, `.envarium/project.yml`, accepted generated
inference, and live deterministic discovery. Retain field-level provenance and
confidence. Unknown fields fail validation. Local overlays never rewrite the
portable manifest.

## Consequences

Users can explain and diff effective values. Merge logic must operate on typed
models rather than generic maps. Schema versions and migrations are explicit,
and proposals remain reviewable until accepted.

---

# ADR-0009: Tauri as a thin desktop shell

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0009-thin-tauri-shell/

Keep native integration in Tauri and product policy in the Go control plane.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Envarium needs a small native desktop experience, tray integration,
notifications, autostart, deep links, and signed updates without duplicating
the control plane.

## Decision

Use Tauri 2 with minimal Rust glue. Bundle the Go binary as a sidecar or attach
to a compatible daemon. All project, runtime, security, and persistence policy
remains in Go application services.

## Consequences

Browser, desktop, CLI, and agents share behavior. Native features are adapters,
not an alternate product core. Sidecar compatibility must be checked before a
desktop client mutates state.

---

# ADR-0010: MCP-first provider-neutral agent integration

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0010-mcp-first-agents/

Give coding agents bounded project context and operations through shared use cases.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Coding agents need stable project context and safe operations without guessing
shell commands or coupling Envarium to one provider.

## Decision

Expose bounded typed resources, prompts, and tools through MCP over shared
application use cases. Keep provider adapters under the agents context behind
provider-neutral interfaces. Core operation remains deterministic without AI.
No generic unrestricted shell tool is part of the MCP surface.

## Consequences

Codex, Claude Code, and other clients receive the same operational vocabulary.
Agent-originated mutations require explicit permissions and audit. Provider
output is untrusted, schema-constrained input requiring validation and human
approval.

---

# ADR-0011: Agent permission profiles and no generic shell tool

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0011-agent-permissions/

Enforce least-privilege agent capabilities independently of prompts.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Agent clients need useful project operations, but prompt content and model
output cannot be trusted as an authorization boundary.

## Decision

Enforce application-level `observe`, `develop`, `maintain`, and `admin`
profiles scoped by provider and project. Default to observe. Annotate MCP tools
with accurate risk/idempotency metadata, audit every agent mutation, and keep
destructive tools disabled by default. Never expose a generic unrestricted
shell MCP tool; agents may invoke only approved typed project actions.

## Consequences

Permissions remain effective independent of prompts or client behavior.
Providers receive less ambient power and users can review agent activity.
Adding a tool requires a use case, risk classification, bounded contract, and
permission tests.

---

# ADR-0012: Versioned out-of-process plugin protocol

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0012-out-of-process-plugins/

Extend Envarium through supervised capability-scoped processes.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Additional runtimes and tools should be extensible without loading untrusted
code into the daemon or coupling core domains to plugin implementations.

## Decision

Plugins run as supervised external processes using a versioned JSON-RPC
protocol. Each declares executable identity, protocol version, capabilities,
and requested scopes. Users explicitly trust and enable plugins. Core domains
depend only on stable application contracts and never import plugin-specific
code.

## Consequences

A plugin crash cannot directly crash the daemon. Serialization, supervision,
capability enforcement, health, compatibility, and conformance testing become
part of the SDK. Shared-library loading and an uncurated automatic marketplace
are out of scope for the core protocol.

---

# ADR-0013: Local IPC and browser session security

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0013-local-transport-security/

Protect privileged local clients and loopback browser mutations.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

CLI, desktop, MCP, and browser clients need local access to privileged
capabilities. Loopback binding alone does not prevent cross-origin requests or
access by other local users.

## Decision

Use user-permissioned Unix sockets on macOS/Linux and named pipes on Windows for
privileged local clients. Serve the browser API on loopback only. A local
bootstrap handshake issues a short-lived same-origin cookie; mutations require
CSRF validation. Validate origins for HTTP and WebSocket traffic, disallow
permissive CORS, expire idle sessions, and audit mutations.

## Consequences

Local clients share handlers while retaining transport-specific authentication.
Socket/pipe cleanup and permissions are tested. Browser JavaScript never
receives the Docker socket or generic process-execution capability.

Current refinements: [ADR-0025](0025-origin-proof-and-reviewed-inputs.md)
supersedes the browser cookie, replay retention and prelaunch compatibility
exceptions where applicable.

---

# ADR-0014: Bounded log retention and redaction

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0014-log-retention-redaction/

Keep log memory and disk bounded while applying one redaction policy to every sink.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Runtime logs are high-volume, may contain credentials, and are consumed live,
persisted, exported, searched, and sent in optional diagnostics or provider
evidence.

## Decision

Keep a bounded in-memory ring per active service and rotating NDJSON files per
run. Store segment identity, time ranges, checksums, and optional indexes in
SQLite. Apply the same configurable redaction pipeline before display,
persistence, export, diagnostics, or AI use. Enforce retention by age and disk
cap and indicate that a value was redacted without exposing it.

## Consequences

Log memory and disk use stay predictable. Redaction correctness is a security
quality gate across every sink. Full-text indexing and compression may be added
without changing the canonical event model.

Current refinements: [ADR-0025](0025-origin-proof-and-reviewed-inputs.md)
supersedes the browser cookie, replay retention and prelaunch compatibility
exceptions where applicable.

---

# ADR-0015: Platform support order

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0015-platform-order/

Implement OS adapters in an explicit order behind platform-neutral contracts.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-15

## Context

Process, port, IPC, PTY, notification, launcher, and packaging behavior differs
substantially by operating system. Attempting simultaneous parity would slow
the product and spread conditionals through domains.

## Decision

Implement and validate macOS first, Linux second, and Windows/WSL third.
Platform-specific behavior lives behind capability interfaces and OS adapter
packages. Domain and application packages remain platform-neutral.

## Consequences

Early releases may have explicitly documented platform gaps. Cross-platform
contracts are designed early but adapters are implemented in roadmap order.
Unsupported capability is a typed, explainable state rather than silent
failure.

---

# ADR-0016: Optional peer federation and signed shared configuration

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0016-optional-federation/

Extend beyond one machine without weakening local-only defaults or ambient authority.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-16

## Context

Envarium v1 deliberately trusts one local user and one local control plane.
Post-v1 demand adds remote development machines, encrypted configuration sync,
team templates, curated plugin metadata, and enterprise policy. Extending the
loopback API over a network would leak ambient local authority, while requiring
a Envarium cloud service would break the local-only product and deployment
model.

## Decision

Add optional peer federation without changing the local control plane's
defaults. A daemon may expose a separate `envarium.remote/v1` agent listener
only when explicitly configured with a server certificate, private key, client
CA, and controller allowlist. The listener requires mutual TLS, pins the
authenticated controller certificate fingerprint, and offers a narrow typed
protocol for identity, bounded inventory, and reviewed project lifecycle
operations. It never exposes the browser session API, terminal streams, raw
logs, secrets, Docker, SQL, plugin processes, MCP, or a generic shell.

The controlling daemon stores machine identity, tunnel HTTPS endpoint,
certificate pin, capabilities, grants, and credential references. It does not
store private credential values. Operators supply the tunnel layer (for
example WireGuard, Tailscale, or an SSH forward); Envarium authenticates and
authorizes both ends independently of tunnel routing. Remote mutations require
an enabled machine, an explicitly granted capability, a matching peer
identity, confirmation for the declared risk, and durable audit on both peers.

Shared configuration uses canonical `envarium.bundle/v1` envelopes. Team
templates, policy packs, curated plugin registries, and enterprise
configuration are signed with Ed25519 and verified against explicitly trusted
publishers before installation. Portable sync archives are encrypted to an
explicit age recipient before leaving a machine. Import is previewable,
conflict-aware, and never includes secret values, repository contents, logs,
terminal output, or runtime state.

Anonymous usage metrics remain disabled by default. Enabling them requires an
explicit HTTPS endpoint and displays the exact bounded aggregate fields.
Existing local workflows never depend on a remote peer, bundle publisher,
telemetry endpoint, or cloud account. The browser provides a responsive
read-only companion view over the controller's already authenticated local
session; it does not create a public web service.

## Consequences

Local-only mode remains the zero-configuration path and all federation code is
behind application ports. Machine outages degrade only remote inventory.
Certificates, signing keys, age identities, and tunnel setup become explicit
operator responsibilities with rotation and revocation procedures.

The direct peer model does not provide rendezvous, NAT traversal, hosted
identity, organization billing, or fleet-wide secret distribution. Those
would be separate products and require new decisions. Remote terminal access
and arbitrary command execution remain intentionally absent.

Current refinements: [ADR-0025](0025-origin-proof-and-reviewed-inputs.md)
supersedes the browser cookie, replay retention and prelaunch compatibility
exceptions where applicable.

---

# ADR-0017: Static public site and documentation portal

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0017-static-public-site/

Keep the public website static, bounded, canonical, and backed by root documentation.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-07-17

## Context

Envarium needs a public product site, documentation portal, download
experience, and contribution funnel. The local Vue application is an
authenticated adapter over privileged daemon capabilities and has a different
deployment, navigation, content, and trust lifecycle from a public website.
The root `docs/` tree already owns product documentation and must not gain a
divergent website copy.

## Decision

Add a separate `site/` pnpm workspace package built with Astro, Starlight, and
strict TypeScript. It produces portable static output with no backend, login,
or runtime database. Starlight loads Markdown directly from the repository
root `docs/` directory. Marketing, releases, documentation, community, SEO,
and design-system code remain explicit site domains; site code may reuse
approved generated tokens and sanitized product screenshots but may not import
Vue stores, generated API clients, or application domain services.

The sole production origin is
`https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech`. Canonical URLs, sitemap entries, feeds,
structured data, and social metadata derive from one typed configuration.
Cloudflare Pages hosts the static output. Preview output is non-indexable, and
the generated Pages production hostname must redirect path-for-path to the
canonical origin through host configuration.

GitHub Releases remains authoritative for binaries. A build-time adapter
normalizes only API-provided asset URLs and fails closed when a published
stable release does not satisfy the versioned release-artifact contract. The
site never proxies binaries or guesses a filename.

The site launches without behavioral analytics. Adding analytics requires a
new explicit data and retention decision.

## Consequences

The public site can be deployed independently without expanding the Go daemon's
attack surface. Documentation remains reviewable beside implementation and can
serve both human and agent-readable forms. Preview deployments and DNS/domain
attachment still require external Cloudflare and GitHub repository settings;
repository progress reports must distinguish those operational checks from
locally verified static output.

---

# ADR-0018: Project-first runtime operations

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0018-project-runtime-operations/

Add deploy, force-stop, service controls, plan confirmation, and operational log tooling without becoming a raw Docker administrator.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-22

## Context

Envarium already owns trusted project lifecycle, runtime observation, durable
operations, health, logs, resources, and activity. Container-management products
such as Arcane demonstrate a useful operational experience: visible service
controls, a redeploy path, detailed inspection, live activity, and capable log
tools. Envarium must provide those workflows for both Compose and native-process
projects without weakening its project-oriented model or exposing Docker and
the host as unrestricted infrastructure APIs.

## Decision

Keep the runtime action vocabulary driver-neutral and add two explicit actions:

- `deploy` reconciles a trusted current definition. Compose runs `up --detach
--pull always --force-recreate --remove-orphans`; native processes perform a
  verified stop and start with the current manifest definition.
- `kill` force-stops selected services. Compose uses `compose kill`; native
  processes verify durable identity fingerprints before force-signalling the
  owned process group.

All project and service lifecycle requests use the same application service,
durable operation coordinator, permission checks, audit path, and typed API.
The UI requests a side-effect-free plan before queueing any lifecycle action,
shows risk, effects, working directories, and exact argument arrays, and sends
an explicit confirmation for execution. Destructive plans are also rejected by
the HTTP boundary when that confirmation is absent.

Service inspection and logs remain read models over existing runtime and
observability domains. UI adapters may filter, pause rendering, expose structured
fields, correlate resource samples, and download existing redacted exports, but
they may not call Docker, SQL, or process execution directly.

Envarium will not add raw container, image, volume, or network CRUD merely to
mirror a Docker administration product. Project definitions, trusted manifests,
storage inventory, cleanup preview, port evidence, and driver adapters remain
the authoritative boundaries. A future raw infrastructure-management mode would
require a separate product decision and threat model.

## Consequences

Users get the operational controls and evidence needed during local development
across both supported runtime drivers. CLI, HTTP, UI, MCP, and remote-machine
adapters share one action contract. Every command remains previewable, bounded,
and auditable. Some Arcane capabilities intentionally map to safer Envarium
equivalents rather than identical Docker resource screens; the complete mapping
is recorded in the Arcane capability review.

---

# ADR-0019: Log memory ownership

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0019-log-memory-ownership/

Bound transient capture memory and use durable replay without a duplicate archive cache.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-16
- Amends: [ADR-0014](0014-log-retention-redaction.md), in-memory ring placement only

## Context

The archive's per-service ring is populated on every append but has no readers:
queries and reconnect replay already read indexed, redacted NDJSON segments.
Native capture separately retains 10,000 entries per run, including all ended
runs for the daemon's lifetime. Entry counts do not bound large message payloads.

## Decision

Keep native capture rings per project/service across runs, bounded by both the configured entry
count (`--log-ring-entries`, default 2,000) and a one-MiB payload budget. Use circular storage so appending a line
does not shift the entire retained history. Run and operation identity remain on
each entry; historical user queries continue through the canonical archive.

Remove the archive's write-only duplicate ring. The existing `--log-ring-entries`
option bounds native capture directly; it does not allocate an archive cache. Subscribers remain bounded and redaction precedes persistence
and fanout. Archive append state retains at most 128 segments and closes segments idle for
one minute, allowing retention to reclaim completed runs. Log maintenance also
runs once per minute without waiting for another producer write.

Terminal scrollback uses a circular byte buffer with the existing one-MiB limit.
Copy scrollback only when attaching, not on every output chunk.

## Consequences

Restart count no longer multiplies native log memory, oversized lines cannot
inflate capture history without a bound, and archive memory does not duplicate
log bodies. Raw native tails share one recent history per service across runs;
durable log queries retain run filters and existing disk policy. Memory still
scales with distinct observed services and live subscriber queues; this is not
a process-wide memory quota. Slow canonical sinks can still exhaust a bounded
capture window, so this change does not promise lossless overload handling.

---

# ADR-0020: Background configuration resolution without CLI polling

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0020-background-configuration-resolution/

Resolve observation metadata in-process while preserving installed-CLI lifecycle validation.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-16
- Refines: ADR-0006 and ADR-0008

## Context

With eleven registered projects and the native app quit, repeated Compose CLI
normalization consumed 6.46% of a CPU core in child processes, in addition to
3.18% daemon CPU. Unchanged manifests were also repeatedly decoded, merged,
and schema-validated by independent observers. Longer polling intervals would
trade freshness for overhead rather than remove the repeated work.

## Decision

Use the official compose-go reference loader in the Compose adapter to resolve
read-only project names and service membership in-process. Continue using the
installed Compose CLI, with fresh normalization, for every lifecycle plan and
execution. Preserve the existing bounded observation refresh window; parsing
errors remain visible and never become a successful empty runtime. Observation
uses local files only, never downloads remote includes or invokes repository
commands. Compare loader metadata with the installed CLI on supported fixtures
and the user's actual projects before deployment.

Read Docker's active context selection and non-secret endpoint metadata from
its local configuration/context store for SDK observation. Preserve context and
environment precedence, verified TLS, explicit errors, and fresh lifecycle CLI
resolution. Read only bounded files; do not read credential helper results or
persist configuration contents.

Memoize effective manifest resolution by exact source contents, including all
precedence layers and runtime overrides. Read current sources before every
lookup, preserve provenance, return independent results, bound retained memory,
and never cache read or validation errors. For persisted accepted snapshots,
a current catalog revision read may identify their immutable contents without
rereading the snapshot body; legacy/unknown revisions use exact content reads.
Local files are always reread before lookup. This memoization has no staleness
window and does not bypass trust, containment, or lifecycle authorization.

Read-only Compose metadata may reuse a previously validated result when exact
contents of all known local inputs and the process environment are unchanged.
Track top-level Compose files, the default dotenv file (including its absence),
and literal service env/label files; reread these inputs within the existing
observation refresh window. Validate before and after loading to avoid retaining
a result across an input race. Includes, extends, dynamically named dependency
files, explicit dotenv modes, and unrecognized dependency syntax fall back to
the reference loader on every refresh. Errors and unsupported graphs are never
memoized. Context selection remains independently fresh. Bound both entries and
tracked input count; retain digests/metadata rather than environment contents.

## Consequences

Background observation no longer requires process creation for unchanged local
Compose projects. The Compose parser is an explicit pinned dependency which
must be updated and tested for compatibility. Installed Compose remains the
lifecycle authority; unsupported remote observation inputs fail explicitly.
No product logic moves to Rust or the UI, and no global mutable cache is added.

Implementation references: [Compose reference loader](https://github.com/compose-spec/compose-go/tree/v2.16.1) and
[Docker context store](https://github.com/docker/cli/tree/v29.4.3/cli/context/store).

---

# ADR-0021: Direct macOS socket inventory with compatibility fallback

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0021-direct-macos-socket-inventory/

Avoid recurring scan subprocesses while retaining kernel port and PID evidence.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-16
- Refines: ADR-0007 and ADR-0015

## Context

After removing lsof, repeated netstat subprocesses still consume approximately
0.32% of a CPU core plus parent process creation and output parsing. The user
requires under 1% combined overhead without reducing monitoring accuracy.

## Decision

Read macOS TCP/UDP PCB inventories directly using the sysctl API used by Apple's
netstat. Decode length/kind tagged records, generation filtering, network-order
ports, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, TCP state and last-owner PID. Keep the existing
observation coalescing window and fresh lifecycle/conflict reads. Revalidate
process fingerprints as before; a socket owner PID is never ownership authority.

These exported records use private ABI definitions. Check every supported record
layout, group completeness, protocol and framing. Fall back to the existing
numeric netstat reader on unavailable APIs, permission errors or unknown layouts;
never turn a decode error into an empty successful inventory. Cancellation stays
visible. Keep input size bounded, and test live IPv4/IPv6 TCP and UDP listeners,
PID attribution, malformed data and comparison with netstat. No cgo or extra
runtime dependency is introduced. Other platforms retain their existing adapter.

## Consequences

Supported macOS versions avoid recurring process creation for monitoring.
Future incompatible kernels retain observation through the compatibility path,
with its original cost. ABI changes require fixture and live-parity verification.
This changes the platform adapter only, not monitoring cadence or product policy.

ABI references: Apple's [netstat reader](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/network_cmds/blob/main/netstat.tproj/inet.c),
[PCB records](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/netinet/in_pcb.h),
[socket records](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/socketvar.h), and
[TCP records](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/netinet/tcp_var.h).

---

# ADR-0022: Bound default daemon CPU execution parallelism

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0022-daemon-execution-parallelism/

Reduce Go scheduler wakeups for the local I/O-oriented control plane.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-17
- Refines: ADR-0002 and ADR-0003

## Context

After eliminating recurring scan subprocesses and redundant configuration/query
work, the actual eleven-project workload still spends a substantial part of CPU
samples waking Go execution threads. The host has twelve logical CPUs; the Go
default chooses twelve execution slots. The user requires under 1% combined
background CPU without weakening monitoring accuracy. A two-slot candidate still
measured 1.09%. The control plane's work is primarily concurrent I/O and short
in-memory computations, not sustained parallel CPU computation.

## Decision

At the CLI daemon composition boundary, default Go CPU execution parallelism to
one slot when GOMAXPROCS has not been explicitly configured. Respect a nonempty
GOMAXPROCS environment override. Restore the previous setting when the daemon
command returns, including startup failure, to isolate embedded CLI/test use.
No other CLI command changes its runtime setting.

This limits simultaneous Go CPU execution, not goroutine concurrency or operating
system threads. Network waits, native process supervision, probe worker limits,
configured probe intervals, runtime/socket reconciliation, metric sampling and
cancellation stay unchanged. Project processes, containers, builds and external
AI/CLI commands remain independent. No CPU percentage limiter or sleep loop is
introduced, and the setting is not changed based on window visibility.

Verify concurrent probe completion, cancellation, actual snapshot latency,
raw sample cadence and workload health before accepting the default. Measure
normal installed binaries in repeated clean windows, including child CPU.

## Consequences

The local daemon avoids excess CPU-worker wakeups in a small I/O workload.
CPU-heavy control-plane operations may take longer; operators needing parallel
Go computation can explicitly configure GOMAXPROCS. This is process runtime
configuration at the composition root, not mutable global product state.
Revisit this default if representative load tests show delayed monitoring or
unacceptable command latency.

---

# ADR-0023: Collect scheduled diagnostic evidence for notification rules

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0023-scheduled-diagnostic-evidence/

Preserve automatic alerts without repeatedly gathering unrelated Git and cleanup recommendations.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-17
- Refines: Phase 17 diagnostic collection

## Context

A longer resource measurement exposed a five-minute CPU spike. The automation
scheduler builds full diagnoses for every trusted project, including Git status
and cleanup recommendations, even when zero automation recipes exist. Git child
commands consumed two CPU seconds in one pass. Simply skipping projects without
recipes would also remove automatic diagnostic notifications, which is not an
acceptable monitoring tradeoff.

## Decision

Keep the five-minute pass for every trusted project, with current runtime,
health, logs, ports, resource warnings, operations, configuration and approved
actions. These inputs cover every notification-producing rule and supported
recipe trigger. Omit Git status and storage cleanup enrichment on scheduled
passes, which feed only non-notifying recommendations. Filter scheduled diagnoses
to notification-producing deterministic hypotheses, so omitted enrichment cannot
create false stale-project or incomplete Git recommendations. Label the omitted
scope explicitly in the saved bundle warnings.

Manual diagnoses, optional AI evidence, and explicit recipe evaluation retain
full collection. Due enabled recipes still use current action permission checks,
cooldowns and daily limits. No recipe or alert is disabled, and no polling,
health, resource or diagnostic cadence changes. Collectors without the optional
scheduled-evidence boundary retain the existing full collection fallback.
Verify parity of all notification codes, summaries and suggested actions between
full and scheduled evidence, plus recipe dispatch and cancellation/error paths.

## Consequences

Routine automatic monitoring no longer runs Git commands or computes unrelated
cleanup recommendations. Full detail remains available on demand. New notifying
rules or recipe triggers must include their dependencies in scheduled evidence
and extend the parity test before acceptance.

---

# ADR-0024: Share observations and isolate resource sampling

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0024-shared-observation-and-sampling-isolation/

Bound presentation-driven work while preserving live monitoring and explicit freshness.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-17
- Refines: ADR-0004, ADR-0006, ADR-0009 and ADR-0022

## Context

With sixteen real containers running, the installed native dashboard consumes
about 67% of one core whether visible or hidden. Most CPU is charged to Git
children. Runtime event invalidations refetch unrelated Git/actions across all
projects and bypass background polling suppression. Metric sampling blocks on
storage scans and reads container statistics sequentially inside a four-second
project deadline; raw history has gaps of up to 39 seconds and unavailable values.

## Decision

Keep runtime, health and metric observation active independently of presentation.
Scope query invalidations to their actual data, use independent shared query
keys for Git/actions/runtime/metrics, and suppress presentation requests while
hidden. Refresh current data when shown. Use document visibility and native
shell visibility/focus signals as presentation facts only (unfocused desktop
presentation also pauses). Suspend the UI event connection while inactive and
resume from its last sequence when shown; tray notifications
and daemon monitoring continue. Transport cancellation reaches the server.

Coalesce concurrent trusted Git requests without weakening trust checks or
caching mutable working-tree status. Reuse immutable commit metadata by HEAD and
validated Git directory discovery; re-read current status, remotes, worktree
inventory and operation markers. Bound retained metadata and copy caller-owned
results. Failed and canceled reads are not successful cache entries.

The dashboard consumes a dedicated fresh working-tree status read; full Git
reads retain commit, remote and worktree enrichment for detail, CLI and MCP
consumers. Give these reads different query/coalescing keys, document omitted
enrichment, and preserve identical trust, branch, edit and operation checks.
The native tray compares only its rendered menu inputs before rebuilding;
snapshot polling and notification processing continue regardless.

Compute the canonical manifest declaration identity once during exact-input
resolution, retaining it internally with the typed copy. Runtime observers use
that identity without repeatedly serializing unchanged declarations. SQLite
footprint reads separate fast counts from indexed oldest-point seeks; rollups
resolve each service's watermark once while retaining late-bucket/idempotent
semantics.

Move storage enrichment onto an independently canceled five-minute worker,
matching the existing storage cache horizon. Metric collection and overview
reads use its latest explicitly partial snapshot and cannot wait for disk scans.
Explicit storage/cleanup preview reads retain their existing inventory behavior.
Collect container statistics with bounded concurrency and serialize sink writes;
one slow container cannot consume the deadline for every later service. Preserve
partial/error reporting and resource intervals. Test freshness, cancellation,
concurrency, failure, scheduling and client isolation.

## Acceptance evidence

Measure the normal installed CLI and native bundle with the same sixteen
containers, counting child CPU and attributable WebKit helpers. Aim for under
1% closed CPU, hidden overhead within 0.5 percentage points of closed, and under
5% visible CPU. Require complete current service metrics and approximately
ten-second raw cadence, including storage refresh and scheduled diagnostics.
Longer memory observations must distinguish RSS from charged footprint and
include sampled transient children. Record achieved values and remaining limits
in the Phase 12 progress log; targets are not hard CPU limits.

The first live candidate still reconciles every Docker health-check exec event.
Ignore only known exec lifecycle chatter in the Compose watcher: it changes
neither container identity nor lifecycle/health state. Continue forwarding actual
health-status, lifecycle, metadata and unknown future events. Resource sampling
and health probes remain independent. This reduces redundant observation and
journal writes without hiding state transitions or inventing longer intervals.

The health scheduler must retain its one-second source checks. Reuse bounded
runtime projections by freshly resolved canonical manifest hash, project root
and slug, rather than cloning actions/provenance and rebuilding identical
runtime declarations. Trust is read before every lookup; current local bytes,
accepted revision, source errors and environment availability/overlays are
checked on every resolution. Retained runtime projections have a four-MiB
weighted budget and 128-entry cap, and returned nested values are copied.

Reuse at most 64 prepared fixed SQL statements / 64 KiB of SQL per SQLite adapter
instance; parameters and result values are never cached. Preparation failures
and canceled requests do not poison later reads, and the database owns statement
closure. Prepare metric inserts/upserts once per transaction rather than once
per point. Keep transaction atomicity, live query semantics and current schema.

The next native probe still spends substantial CPU in per-project HTTP traffic
and the Apple Git launcher. Batch presentation reads by kind (runtime, Git
status, or actions), with at most 64 unique IDs, four application-service calls
in flight, ordered results, explicit per-project warnings and cancellation.
Each owning service retains current permission/freshness checks. Separate
kind-specific TanStack Query keys prevent runtime events from refetching Git.
Single-project detail/CLI/MCP reads retain their APIs. The dashboard resource
sampler remains independent. Refresh all current facts on an event replay gap.

Connected idle operation presentation uses event invalidation plus a fifteen-
second safety poll; active operations and disconnected presentation retain the
1.5-second poll. Native sidecars request compact JSON to avoid per-line subprocess
framing overhead, retaining the exact envelope. Resolve Apple's selected Git
toolchain once per observer instead of invoking its launcher for every status;
honor custom PATH and fall back if the selected executable disappears.

Host presentation consumes the resource worker's cached disk summary rather
than initiating a second Docker filesystem traversal. Unknown storage remains
unknown; a cheap ping can still report Engine connectivity. Explicit disk reads
and the independent five-minute enrichment worker retain their behavior.

Each scheduled diagnostic cycle captures global port/resource read models once
through an explicit scoped collector; project trust, health, logs and approved
actions remain independently current. Global-source failures remain partial
warnings in each affected bundle. Interactive collection retains its own reads.
Health history seeks the latest indexed row per check, preserving timestamp/ID
tie-breaking and all check scopes, instead of ranking every historical payload.

Apply the existing one-core I/O execution budget at the CLI process entry as
well as daemon entry, respecting explicit GOMAXPROCS overrides. Only the current
Go runtime is configured: environment variables are unchanged, so autostarted
daemons and project subprocesses retain their own configured/default settings.

Incremental metric rollups enumerate source series, seek each target watermark,
and read each source's indexed timestamp range. Keep the existing schema,
chronological input order, per-series watermarks, late-current-bucket behavior
and idempotent upserts. Do not scan all retained payload rows merely to discard
those preceding the watermark.

Only runtime status observation requests Docker server-version metadata.
Metrics, log and event connections retain API negotiation and report their own
request failures without fetching unused version payloads. Read exact resource
footprint aggregates in one SQLite snapshot, retaining independent COUNT and
indexed MIN plans while avoiding repeated WAL lock acquisition.

Native tray snapshots use a bounded `status` batch containing the same current
runtime and health facts, rather than two HTTP requests per project. Health
reconciliation of degraded/starting runtime states belongs to the shared
application read used by both single-project HTTP and batched readers. Preserve
per-project partial warnings, current trust checks, notification inputs and the
fifteen-second native polling interval. Older daemons may use the existing
single-project fallback when the additive batch kind is unsupported.

Reuse at most eight idle Docker SDK clients for explicit local Unix endpoints,
owned by the Compose driver and closed on shutdown. Each active lease has its
own client; all API negotiation, status metadata and runtime/metric requests stay
fresh. Environment-selected and non-Unix/TLS connections keep fresh clients so
credential/environment changes cannot be hidden by pooling. Failed negotiation
discards its client. Bound retained clients across all endpoint identities;
returning a lease after shutdown closes it immediately.

Treat query payloads as immutable replacement values: use shallow Vue Query
state for dashboard/host/operation reads, and disable their presentation timers
while inactive. Skip global invalidation timers when an event changes none of
the subscribed read models. Retain monitoring and native notification polling.

Bound the native notification adapter's recently seen operation identities to
1,024 entries. Cache fixed health write plans under the same database statement
budget, without caching result values. Reuse the already serialized log entry's
size when computing its fingerprint rather than serializing it again solely to
estimate segment rotation.

Contain dashboard-card layout and painting within each card, preserving its
intrinsic sizing, keyboard controls and existing visual hierarchy. Validate
desktop/narrow/hover rendering and actual native performance before accepting.

Resolve sibling optional manifests through one confined, identity-checked
directory handle per resolution. Read each current file and validate its opened
descriptor and byte cap independently; retain no directory or byte cache across
resolutions. A missing directory is checked again on the next resolution.
This removes repeated parent walks without allowing symlink aliases or stale
manifest contents.

Read registered environments and their exact leases in one adapter-owned SQL
snapshot. Scheduler snapshots may consume a typed batch of those current
environment allocations instead of listing them and immediately fetching each
one again. Preserve independent direct lifecycle reads, per-target trust and
availability checks, caller-owned maps, cancellation and explicit errors.

Drive background health, event-subscription reconciliation and log inventory from
one fresh one-second project observation feed. Each subscriber owns a copied,
bounded latest snapshot; slow consumers do not block monitoring or queue stale
cycles. Failed cycles remain explicit. Direct requests and lifecycle execution
continue resolving current trust and files independently. The feed has an
explicit daemon-owned lifetime and retains no interactive query cache. This
preserves the fastest existing configuration check cadence while eliminating
independent duplicate catalog, manifest and environment reads.

On Darwin and Linux, traverse manifest parent directories using pinned directory
file descriptors and kernel-enforced `openat(O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW)` boundaries.
This replaces redundant pre/post directory stats with an atomic no-symlink
open, while retaining pre-open regular-file checks, nonblocking/no-follow file
opens, opened-descriptor identity checks and post-read byte caps. Synchronize
close against opens to prevent descriptor reuse from changing the capability.
Other platforms retain the rooted Go filesystem implementation. Retain no
handles or bytes between observations, and verify symlink, FIFO, replacement,
close/cancellation and cross-platform behavior before accepting the change.

Native process watchers retain their two-second reconciliation cadence and
immediate lifecycle events, but share one fresh batch of durable run records per
cycle. Batch only through the run store's explicit domain interface (at most 64
project IDs per SQL read); preserve the newest 200 runs per project and every
stored fingerprint. Each subscriber receives owned values, failed reads stop
that watch explicitly, slow subscribers retain only the latest cycle, and the
feed stops when its final watcher exits. Do not cache run results between cycles
or weaken PID/group ownership verification.

Resolve current trusted runtime inputs once per combined health or resource
read. The runtime application service can return both its resolved project and
current observation, or observation plus statistics, to the owning monitoring
adapter. Reuse only that call's typed inputs; preserve direct trust/file checks,
active/inactive classification, existing status coalescing, driver failures and
metric sampling. Alternate adapters retain their existing independent reads.

Native port attribution is also an explicit inventory concern: a process being
alive does not prove every configured socket exists. The native driver exposes
an on-demand binding read that intersects current TCP listeners with freshly
verified run/process-group owners and retains actual IPv4/IPv6 addresses. The
port registry uses that application boundary. Its failures do not alter ordinary
runtime, health or metric observations, and no background socket poll is added.

The Compose metric cycle can share a single current container inventory and each
successful post-statistics inspection with status assembly. Its evidence map is
owned by that call and discarded immediately afterward. It is never an aged
restart-count cache: every new sample cycle reads new Engine statistics and
inspections, stopped containers do no statistics work, partial failures remain
explicit, and the pre-inventory ownership token still guards reconciliation.
Direct lifecycle inspection and planning retain their existing fresh paths.

Keep the native tray snapshot a presentation DTO containing the actual menu and
notification inputs. Do not serialize full runtime service inventories,
repository paths, workspace recipes or operation details that the native shell
does not consume. Preserve system/host values, project state and health,
workspace identities, operation transitions, notification contents, conflicts
and unavailable observations. This does not change the public HTTP contract or
ordinary CLI views, nor any observation source or interval.

The short-lived `desktop snapshot` child limits Go parallelism to one and skips
percentage-triggered collection while retaining a 64 MiB soft runtime memory
limit. A read-only benchmark against sixteen running containers reduced child
CPU by about 25% and output from 34 KiB to 7 KiB without increasing peak RSS.
Apply these environment overrides only to that exact leaf command; daemon
startup, UI initialization and mutations retain their ordinary runtime policy.
Tests enforce that boundary. The daemon and managed processes never inherit
these overrides.

The native shell may retain one read-only `desktop snapshot --stream` bridge
instead of launching a process for each fifteen-second tray refresh. Each exact
`snapshot` input line requests the same fresh application reads, with a bounded
deadline and one bounded envelope; no timer or mutation policy moves into Rust.
EOF/cancellation closes the bridge. Native failure, invalid output or timeout
discards the owned child and reconnects on the next ordinary poll. Keep normal
GC and a soft memory limit for this longer-lived adapter. Daemon startup and
mutations never inherit its resource policy. Shared presentation queries must
also share their observer/timer, not merely a query cache key. Card rendering
may skip timestamp-only changes while retaining every displayed value and live
action inputs. Monitoring and presentation freshness intervals stay unchanged.

---

# ADR-0025: Origin proof and immutable reviewed inputs

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0025-origin-proof-and-reviewed-inputs/

Close cross-port browser replay and bind external disclosure to reviewed bytes.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-18
- Refines: ADR-0013, ADR-0014 and ADR-0016

## Context

Cookies ignore TCP ports. A development server sharing the browser API's
loopback hostname can receive its cookie. Cookie possession must therefore
never independently authorize API reads or interactive WebSocket attachment.
Live repository files and imported configuration can also change after review.

## Decision

Require the session's origin-scoped proof on every browser API request,
including reads and side-effect-free plans. Do not issue bearer session cookies.
Keep the bootstrap-issued proof in origin-scoped session
storage, send it as X-CSRF-Token for HTTP, and offer it in an authentication
WebSocket subprotocol before attachment. Negotiate only the public
`envarium.v1` protocol so browser handshakes complete. Never negotiate/echo the secret or
place it in URLs. Preserve same-origin checks, idle/absolute expiry, IPC bootstrap and
terminal ownership. Invalid proof must not extend session lifetime.

External evidence dispatch and trust-changing imports require the digest of
the reviewed canonical input. Revalidate before dispatch/import and reject
changed input rather than silently using new bytes. New consent is required
after provider, limits or payload changes.

Repository readers use rooted filesystem operations, regular-file validation,
nonblocking opens on Unix and hard byte caps. Evidence reads reject symlinked
sources rather than allowing aliases to bypass sensitive-path policy. Current
valid manifest edits remain observable; immutable caches do not hide changes.

Remote capabilities derive from a resolved target, with an environment bound
to its actual parent project. Current signed policy restricts reads as well as
mutations, including inventory fetched to validate an operation target.
Workspace operation authorization uses immutable submitted members, and
execution requires the reviewed workspace revision. Unsupported policy promises must not be presented as enforced.

The replay journal retains the latest 100,000 sequence positions, pruning on
startup's first publish and every 1,024 events. Clients older than the retained
window must refresh authoritative state. Audit records and resource history
have separate ownership and are not pruned by this policy. Freed SQLite pages
are reused; no blocking full-database VACUUM runs in monitoring paths.

The prelaunch alpha manifest reader/migrator and old-daemon status fallback
are retired. Only the stable manifest contract is accepted. Ordered database
migrations remain intact for the active installation. This supersedes the
earlier phase-18 prelaunch compatibility policy.

Signed configuration is mandatory for all team bundles, so there is no optional
`requireSignedConfiguration` switch. The registry publisher allowlist is named
`allowedRegistryPublishers` and restricts curated registry metadata. Explicit
local trust of a native plugin remains a separate owner-level decision; this
policy does not claim to sandbox native code.

## Consequences

Cookies carry no browser authority. Browser
clients must send proof on reads and WebSockets; privileged IPC is unchanged.
Reviewed-input digests are additive contract changes enforced fail-closed.
Adversarial special files, changed input, expired sessions and rejected scopes
receive regression coverage alongside ordinary workflows.

---

# ADR-0026: Reviewed checkout transitions

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0026-reviewed-checkout-transitions/

Keep Git branch changes and runtime restarts explicit, serialized and recoverable.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-17
- Refines: ADR-0001, ADR-0008, ADR-0013, ADR-0024

## Decision

Expose detailed changed-file and local-branch inventory only on explicit request.
Keep dashboard and scheduled diagnostic Git reads small. Preserve literal NUL-
delimited filenames, independent index/working-tree status and bounded results.

Switch only existing local branches in a trusted, clean, stopped checkout. A
review binds the source branch/HEAD and target branch/HEAD; execution rereads
those facts and rejects changes, conflicts, in-progress operations and branches
used by another worktree. Never force checkout, discard edits, stash, fetch or
recurse into submodules. Disable hooks and fsmonitor; reject configured checkout
filters rather than running repository-selected programs. Preserve ignored files
with Git's no-overwrite-ignore mode.

Use durable, actor-audited operations. Agent-originated branch mutation is denied;
local users review the exact transition. Runtime mutations and checkout changes
share a root-scoped application gate, including a primary registered environment
that shares the checkout. Fresh driver observations must prove that checkout's
runtime is stopped. A runtime plan created before a checkout/configuration change
cannot subsequently execute unchanged under the same gate.

Switching leaves the runtime stopped. Offer a new lifecycle preview using the
new branch's current configuration, requiring a separate restart confirmation.
Do not execute newly checked-out commands based on approval of the old branch.
An interrupted or failed Git operation remains visible and is never silently
rolled back or retried. Existing non-primary worktrees retain isolated runtime
identities and explicit start/restart/stop previews.

Bind browser runtime confirmation and queued execution to the manifest identity
and a daemon-owned checkout revision. A root-scoped revision changes after every
attempted Envarium checkout mutation, even if the Git operation fails partway.
Revisions are opaque random identities: daemon restart or eviction of an idle
entry invalidates old reviews. Retain at most 128 root entries and never evict
an in-flight root. This adds no background Git polling. Normal source edits stay
part of the development workflow; this revision specifically binds Envarium's
managed checkout transition, while current manifest inputs are checked afresh.

---

# ADR-0027: Native worktree ownership and reviewed transitions

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/adr/0027-native-worktree-runtimes/

Isolate native runtime ownership and exact ports across trusted checkouts.

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-18
- Refines: ADR-0007, ADR-0008, ADR-0026

## Decision

Keep the catalog project as the durable foreign-key owner of native runs, while
persisting a separate runtime scope identity. A base checkout and each registered
worktree have separate process groups, runs, logs, metrics and lifecycle gates.
Keep health history scoped and log segment metadata catalog-owned as well.
Migrate existing runs without changing their scope or fingerprints. Never create
fake catalog projects to satisfy a run foreign key.

Resolve portable/local manifest inputs from the selected registered checkout,
using the trusted base project's accepted inference as fallback. Bind previews to
that checkout's current configuration and exact allocated ports. Cache projections
per project and root with the existing memory bounds; no additional background
Git or socket polling is introduced. Worktree discovery updates metadata without
overwriting newer runtime routing state or exact leases; unchanged allocations
need no runtime write.

Native commands and environment values may explicitly reference `${ports.ID}`.
Resolve only known declarations to decimal host-port values; never infer and
rewrite arbitrary numeric arguments. A native worktree's declared service ports
must be consumed by that service's effective command/environment, or its start
preview fails with an actionable error. Keep executable and working-directory
selection explicit; reject worktree working directories outside the selected
checkout. Preserve argument arrays and existing shell opt-in.

Use the same local-user-only branch review for registered worktrees. Checkout
changes remain stopped, clean, ref-bound, hook/filter-free and serialized with
runtime actions. The interface guides stop, checkout, and fresh start reviews;
approval of old-branch commands never authorizes newly checked-out commands.
Switching services between existing worktrees stops only the selected source and
reviews a fresh target restart. Other worktrees remain independent. Cancellation
or failure stops the workflow and is visible; do not silently roll back checkout
changes or retry commands from another branch. Pending crash restart backoff
counts as active ownership; stop/kill cancel and join the supervised restart
before checkout mutation. A fully exited failed runtime is quiescent, while
starting, restarting and unknown states remain blocked.

Native friendly HTTP routes require a currently observed, ownership-verified TCP
binding at an exact leased port. Declarations and a live PID alone cannot publish
a route. Existing Compose isolation remains unchanged.

## Acceptance evidence required

Exercise two native worktrees simultaneously with SQLite persistence, distinct
ports, branch-specific responses, scoped restart/stop/logs/metrics and daemon
reconciliation. Verify stale reviews, trust revocation, unknown/fixed ports,
occupied ports, cancellation and failed transitions. Test the complete reviewed
browser workflow on owned repositories; preserve the user's running projects.
Run migrations, generated-artifact checks, full quality suites, rebuild/install,
and exact-master hosted CI before handoff. Record evidence in Phase 13.

---

# Architecture overview

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/architecture/

Process topology, bounded contexts, dependency direction, and accepted Envarium decisions.

Envarium is a local-first modular monolith delivered primarily as one Go
binary. The process hosts a daemon, CLI commands, local HTTP/WebSocket and IPC
transports, and an MCP façade. A Vue application and thin Tauri desktop shell
consume the same application behavior.

The [durable operations and local transport](operations-kernel.md) note defines
the command state machine, restart behavior, event replay, Unix IPC, and browser
session handshake introduced by Phase 2.

The [project onboarding and manifest resolution](project-onboarding.md) note
defines the Phase 3 repository trust boundary, evidence pipeline, approval
transaction, generated schema, and configuration precedence.

The [Docker Compose runtime](docker-compose-runtime.md) and
[native process runtime](native-process-runtime.md) notes describe the two
initial lifecycle drivers, their evidence models, and their ownership limits.
The [health, log, and resource observability](observability.md) note defines the
redaction boundary, rotating storage, cursor replay, health scheduling,
degraded-state derivation, metric tiers, and storage-attribution boundary
introduced by Phases 7 and 12.
The [ports, source control, and trusted actions](developer-workflows.md) note
defines Phase 8 port provenance and reservations, read-only Git observation,
action authorization, working-directory containment, and audit recovery.
The [dashboard alpha](dashboard-alpha.md) note defines Phase 9 routes, server
state ownership, command boundaries, degraded behavior, and browser evidence.
The [agent integration](agent-integration.md) note defines Phase 10 MCP
topology, least-privilege discovery, audit identity, provider installers, and
failure isolation.
The [AI-assisted onboarding](ai-assisted-onboarding.md) note defines Phase 11
evidence consent, provider isolation, schema-constrained output, deterministic
merge authority, dry-run review, and human-only trust transitions.
The [workspace and worktree orchestration](workspaces.md) note defines Phase 13
dependency execution, failure policy, environment isolation, optional local
routing, launch recipes, and restart reconciliation.
The [embedded terminal and agent sessions](terminal-sessions.md) note defines
Phase 14 PTY ownership, typed launch resolution, authenticated binary streams,
detach persistence, bounded scrollback, and the user-visible agent metadata
boundary.
The [native desktop shell](desktop-shell.md) note defines Phase 15 sidecar
attachment, compatibility gates, native adapter ownership, capability
isolation, notification transitions, and signed update behavior.
The [out-of-process plugin architecture](plugins.md) note defines Phase 16
discovery, executable trust, JSON-RPC negotiation, capability enforcement,
supervision, and local-user security boundaries. The public
[plugin SDK guide](../plugin-sdk.md) documents authoring and compatibility.
The [intelligent diagnostics and safe automation](intelligent-diagnostics.md)
note defines Phase 17 bounded evidence, deterministic-first evaluation,
provider validation, prompt-injection resistance, action authorization,
rate-limited recipes, local feedback, and notification retention.
The [optional federation guide](../federation.md),
[signed team configuration guide](../team-configuration.md), and ADR-0016 define
Phase 19's separate peer identity, mutual-TLS authorization, bounded inventory,
signed portable policy, encrypted sync, curated metadata, and explicit
anonymous-counter consent boundaries.

## Process topology

```text
CLI          Browser/Vue          Tauri          MCP clients
 |                |                 |                 |
 +---------- local IPC / loopback HTTP / stdio -------+
                              |
                   transport adapters
                              |
                   application use cases
                              |
                       domain modules
                              |
          focused infrastructure adapter interfaces
               /        |        |        \
           SQLite     Docker   processes   Git/OS
```

The daemon owns project truth. Clients never call Docker, SQL, or operating
system process APIs directly. Tauri/Rust contains packaging and native-shell
integration only.

## Dependency direction

```text
transport and UI adapters -> application -> domain
infrastructure adapters ----- implement ---> application ports
```

A domain owns its model, invariants, use cases, persistence interfaces, and
adapter contracts. Domain code must not import transport, database, Docker,
operating-system command, desktop, or AI-provider packages. A domain cannot
read another domain's tables. Cross-domain behavior uses an explicit
application interface or a typed event.

## Bounded contexts

| Context | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `catalog` | Projects, locations, tags, and trust/approval |
| `manifest` | Configuration, overlays, provenance, proposals, schema versions |
| `operations` | Durable operations, progress, cancellation, serialization |
| `runtime` | Driver contracts, runs, reconciliation, lifecycle execution |
| `observability` | Logs, health, events, metrics, and retention |
| `ports` | Declarations, reservations, bindings, conflicts, and leases |
| `sourcecontrol` | Git repository facts and worktrees |
| `actions` | Typed, risk-classified project actions |
| `workspace` | Multi-project graphs and coordinated lifecycle |
| `agents` | MCP, provider adapters, proposals, sessions, and agent audit |
| `diagnostics` | Bounded evidence, deterministic findings, reviewed suggestions, local feedback, alerts, and automation policy |
| `terminal` | Owned PTYs, bounded streams, typed interactive launches, and session audit |
| `plugins` | External package discovery, executable trust, scopes, supervision, and typed actions |
| `fleet` | Authenticated peer identities, bounded inventory, grants, remote operations, and audit |
| `team` | Publisher trust, signed portable bundles, restrictive policy, registry metadata, and encrypted sync |
| `telemetry` | Explicit consent, fixed anonymous counters, payload preview, delivery, and opt-out deletion |
| `settings` | Revisioned local preferences, safe project roots, adapter choices, and restart-effect reporting |
| `platform` | OS capabilities without product policy |

`foundation` is limited to stable primitives such as clocks, IDs, event
envelopes, pagination, and problem details. It is not a miscellaneous shared
code layer. Root packages named `utils`, `common`, or `helpers` are forbidden.

## Composition

Construct dependencies explicitly at a small composition root. Interfaces live
with their consumer and exist only for a real boundary, alternate adapter, or
test seam. Long-running work receives a context, has defined cancellation, and
records progress and outcome. Architecture checks enforce dependency rules.

Accepted decisions and their consequences are indexed in
[`docs/adr`](../adr/README.md).

---

# Agent integration

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/architecture/agent-integration/

Provider-neutral MCP, permission, audit, guidance, and agent-session architecture.

Envarium exposes the same application use cases used by its CLI and browser
through a permission-scoped Model Context Protocol server. The MCP process is a
stdio adapter; the durable daemon remains the owner of catalog, runtime,
operation, health, log, port, Git, and action state.

```text
Codex / Claude Code / MCP client
              |
       MCP stdio process
     profile + project scope
              |
   authenticated local IPC client
       actor=provider/agent
              |
       Envarium daemon
              |
 shared application use cases -> durable operations and audit
```

The MCP adapter does not import runtime drivers, persistence adapters, or
`os/exec`. A failed or disconnected MCP process cannot terminate the daemon or
degrade ordinary CLI and browser access.

## Authorization

Tool discovery is itself least-privilege. A server instance receives one
validated provider, agent identity, permission profile, and optional project
allowlist at startup. Tools outside that profile are not registered.

| Profile | Capabilities |
|---|---|
| `observe` | Bounded project, runtime, health, logs, Git, ports, actions, manifest, and operation reads |
| `develop` | Observe plus start, stop, restart, force-stop, pause, resume, trusted actions, and operation cancellation |
| `maintain` | Develop plus deploy, rebuild, and deterministic manifest proposal creation |
| `admin` | Maintain plus proposal acceptance, destructive trusted actions, and teardown |

The default is `observe`. Destructive tools are therefore absent unless the
MCP server is explicitly configured with `admin`. Project allowlists apply to
reads, port-conflict evidence, and mutations. A project-scoped server cannot
register another project, and proposal IDs are resolved to their owning project
before trust authorization. Every mutation uses a caller-supplied idempotency key and
reaches the daemon over local IPC with `agent` and `provider/agent` identity
headers. Operation and catalog audit records persist that non-secret origin.

## Protocol behavior

- Tool inputs and structured outputs are generated by the official Go MCP SDK.
- Every output includes `schemaVersion: envarium.mcp/v1`.
- Lists, logs, resources, ports, services, and recent errors have hard bounds.
- Log content has already crossed the daemon's redaction boundary.
- Operation and health waits are limited to 30 seconds and emit MCP progress
  notifications when the client supplies a progress token.
- Cancellation requests are cooperative durable operations, not process kills.
- Risk and idempotency annotations describe each tool; trusted action risk is
  re-read from the accepted manifest immediately before submission.
- There is no generic shell, Docker-command, SQL, or process-execution tool.

Repository evidence, manifest content, logs, and action output remain untrusted
data. Shared prompts and installed Agent Skills explicitly tell clients not to
follow instructions embedded in that data and not to bypass Envarium with
ad hoc shell commands.

## Provider installation

`envarium agent install codex` manages a marked MCP block in
`.codex/config.toml`, installs the shared skill under
`.agents/skills/envarium-operate`, and adds a marked `AGENTS.md` block.

`envarium agent install claude` merges the `envarium` stdio server into
`.mcp.json`, installs the same policy as a Claude skill under
`.claude/skills/envarium-operate`, adds the shared `AGENTS.md` block, and
ensures `CLAUDE.md` imports `@AGENTS.md`.

Both installers preserve unrelated configuration, reject unsafe file types or
malformed managed markers, write atomically, and are idempotent. User-level
installation is available with `--scope user`; project scope is the default.

## Verification

SDK in-memory tests exercise initialize, tool/resource/prompt discovery,
structured calls, permission omission, scoped reads, lifecycle submission,
operation waits, and destructive denial. The pinned MCP Inspector smoke test
starts a real daemon and real stdio server, then lists tools, resources, and
prompts while asserting the observe profile omits teardown.

---

# AI-assisted onboarding

Source: https://envarium.davidcuellar.tech/docs/architecture/ai-assisted-onboarding/

Bounded evidence, schema-constrained proposals, validation, and human approval.

Phase 11 adds an optional provider step after deterministic discovery. AI is a
proposal source, not an authority: the deterministic scanner remains usable
with every provider disabled, and only the catalog's ordinary human approval
transaction can create a trusted manifest snapshot.

## Boundary and data flow

```text
deterministic proposal
        |
        v
bounded structural sanitizer + canonical redactor
        |
        +--> exact JSON preview, byte count, redaction count, SHA-256 receipt
        |
        v
provider-neutral ProposalProvider
        |
        v
JSON Schema validation + evidence-ID verification
        |
        v
typed merge + dry-run + immutable untrusted proposal revision
        |
        v
browser/CLI human approval
```

The evidence bundle contains relative source paths, exact source ranges,
structured deterministic findings, bounded excerpts, the deterministic
candidate, confidence, and unresolved fields. It never contains the selected
absolute repository root. Environment values, secret-reference keys and
accounts, common credential formats, configured redaction patterns, and known
secret values are removed before preview, persistence, or dispatch. `.env`,
secret-named files, and full existing manifests are never excerpted.

The preview's `encoded` object is byte-for-byte the JSON sent to the provider.
The run stores the same bytes and their SHA-256 digest. Raw provider output is
validated and discarded; it is not persisted as a log or diagnostic payload.

## Provider isolation

All providers implement the consumer-owned `ProposalProvider` interface under
`internal/agents/application`. Provider-specific protocol code stays under
`internal/agents/providers`.

- Codex runs with `exec`, `--sandbox read-only`, an empty temporary working
  root, ephemeral sessions, ignored user configuration/rules, and
  `--output-schema`. The prompt travels on stdin, not argv.
- Claude Code runs in print mode with plan permissions, bare/no-session mode,
  an empty tool set, an empty temporary working root, `--json-schema`, and
  explicit turn/cost limits.
- The OpenAI-compatible adapter calls only the daemon-configured endpoint and
  model. It uses Chat Completions Structured Outputs, disables redirects,
  disables proxies for plaintext local endpoints, rejects URL credentials,
  and permits plaintext HTTP only for localhost or private IP literals.

CLI subprocesses inherit an allowlist rather than the daemon environment. A
repository cannot select or shadow the executable: bare command names resolve
only through absolute `PATH` entries, and configured paths must be absolute.
Provider stderr and HTTP errors are bounded and redacted.

The daemon flags are:

```text
--ai-codex-executable /absolute/path/or/bare-name
--ai-codex-model optional-model
--ai-claude-executable /absolute/path/or/bare-name
--ai-claude-model optional-model
--ai-openai-endpoint https://provider.example/v1
--ai-openai-model configured-model
--ai-openai-api-key-env OPENAI_API_KEY
```

The API key value is read only from the named process environment variable and
is never persisted or returned. Local endpoints may omit it.

## Merge and approval policy

Providers return a complete candidate plus claims at a fixed set of JSON
Pointers. Claims may reference only evidence IDs present in the sent bundle.
Envarium computes confidence from those evidence records and caps provider
confidence below deterministic authority; model-reported confidence is not
accepted.

High-confidence deterministic values are retained and surfaced as conflicts
with `kept_deterministic` resolution. New commands, process definitions,
actions, Compose files/services, ports, and endpoints must exactly match
deterministic evidence. Provider requests for shell execution, environment
